statement: Kernel-checked; advisory statement coverage pending. For a finite-dimensional unit torus sequence whose every nonzero integer Fourier average tends to zero, empirical measures converge weakly to normalized Haar measure. Counts of every Borel set with Haar-null frontier, divided by N, tend to its Haar measure. For real fractional parts and fixed 0<=a_i<b_i<=1, every half-open product box has frequency product_i(b_i-a_i), including a_i=0 and b_i=1. Circle-arc volumes and null boundaries are proved; no box-frequency premise is assumed.

Kernel-checked; advisory statement coverage pending. Distinct positive noninteger real powers of A*t+B, A>0, with nonzero real scales have each fixed half-open box's volume as parameter frequency. If P has parameter density delta, and natural q,d>0, the number of distinct starts (1+q*t)^d<=X with P(t), divided by X^(1/d), tends to delta/q. The exact cutoff and injectivity are proved. For delta>0 and fixed c>1 every sufficiently large (X,cX] contains such a start. Finite changes of P preserve density. No effective rate is asserted.
